name: The Trevor Project
summary: 24/7 crisis support for LGBTQ+ young people experiencing mental health crisis or suicidal thoughts.

sections.title: About The Trevor Project
sections.text: The Trevor Project is the world's largest suicide prevention and mental health organization for LGBTQ+ young people. Founded in 1998 after the Academy Award-winning short film 'Trevor,' the organization provides 24/7 crisis intervention and suicide prevention services to LGBTQ+ young people under 25 through phone, text, and chat. The Trevor Project has answered millions of contacts and trains thousands of counselors each year.

sections.title: Who Should Reach Out
sections.text: The Trevor Project serves LGBTQ+ young people under 25 who are experiencing crisis, thinking about suicide, or simply need someone to talk to. Common reasons to reach out include feeling isolated, experiencing rejection from family or friends, dealing with bullying, questioning gender identity or sexual orientation, struggling with anxiety or depression, or needing support during difficult times. You don't have to identify any specific way to reach out.

sections.title: How to Contact The Trevor Project
sections.text: Call the TrevorLifeline at 1-866-488-7386 available 24/7. Text START to 678-678 for TrevorText. Chat online at TheTrevorProject.org/get-help. All services are free, confidential, and staffed by trained LGBTQ+ counselors who understand your experiences. Average wait times are typically under 5 minutes. Spanish-speaking support is available.

sections.title: TrevorSpace Online Community
sections.text: Beyond crisis services, The Trevor Project offers TrevorSpace, an affirming international online community for LGBTQ+ young people ages 13-24. TrevorSpace is a monitored social networking site where young people can connect with peers, share their stories, find support, and access resources in a safe environment. The community has helped thousands of LGBTQ+ youth feel less alone.

sections.title: Education and Training
sections.text: The Trevor Project provides free educational resources including guides for parents of LGBTQ+ youth, resources for educators and schools, workplace training programs, and research on LGBTQ+ youth mental health. Their annual National Survey on LGBTQ+ Youth Mental Health provides vital data that informs policy and programs. The organization also advocates for LGBTQ+ youth at local, state, and federal levels.
